facts.statement: When collecting a directory argument, the session visits its descendant paths and, once per encountered directory, explicitly looks for __init__.py and passes any existing initializer to _collectfile before ordinary file collection.
The Python collection hook accepts .py files matching configured python_files patterns plus an unconditional extra __init__.py pattern, then creates a Python module collector for them.
pytest_pycollect_makemodule maps a collected __init__.py specifically to a Package collector rather than a regular Module collector.
Package.collect mounts the package object before traversing package contents; mounting obtains the object through the inherited module-loading path.
Module's object-loading implementation imports its filesystem path with pyimport, so mounting a Package whose fspath is __init__.py executes that initializer during collection.
The import implementation converts SyntaxError and ImportError raised while importing a collected module into collection errors.

The Package collector only yields its own __init__.py as a Module when that initializer matches the configured python_files patterns, but this check occurs after Package.collect has already mounted and therefore imported the package object.
Existing tests explicitly cover collecting tests from __init__.py when python_files is configured to match them and cover directly passing an __init__.py as the collection argument.
An existing test records the expected behavior that __init__.py is not collected as a test module when it does not match python_files.

scope_summary: Base commit e856638ba086fcf5bebf1bebea32d5cf78de87b4 contains collection logic that discovers package initializers during directory traversal, treats every Python __init__.py as collectable, and imports package initializers when their Package collectors run.
unknowns: No repository test located in the inspected collection tests directly covers a non-test package __init__.py that raises merely because pytest was invoked on an ancestor directory.
